query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount (1–2 at.%) of Nb to the eutectic AlCoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy, followed by controlled slow cooling, will promote the in situ formation of coherent Nb-rich nanoprecipitates at the lamellar colony boundaries. This microalloying intervention is hypothesized to strengthen the boundaries by blocking crack initiation and dislocation motion, thereby simultaneously enhancing room-temperature tensile strength and ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar architecture.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high‐entropy alloy (AlCoCrFeNi-based system) with dual-phase lamellar colonies featuring sharp internal boundaries that are prone to microcrack initiation and brittle failure under room-temperature tensile loading.
generation.intervention: Microalloying with trace Nb addition during melting (1–2 at.%) followed by controlled slow cooling.
generation.conditions: The base alloy is melted with a 1–2 at.% Nb addition under vacuum induction melting. The cast alloy is then subjected to controlled slow cooling to ensure the segregation of Nb at the lamellar boundaries and promote the formation of fine, coherent Nb-rich nanoprecipitates without triggering deleterious second phases.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of uniformly distributed, coherent Nb-rich nanoprecipitates along the interphase (lamellar colony) boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Nb segregates to the internal boundaries during slow cooling where it forms nanoscale, coherent precipitates. These precipitates serve a dual role: they obstruct dislocation motion (thereby increasing strength via precipitation hardening) and they toughen the boundaries by blunting potential crack tips, reducing local stress concentrations and suppressing microcrack initiation during tensile deformation.
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified alloy is expected to exhibit an increase in both yield/ultimate tensile strength and room-temperature ductility. Compared to the unmodified lamellar structure, the Nb-enhanced alloy should show a reduction in microcrack formation and propagation, resulting in a more uniform deformation behavior under tensile loading.
generation.baseline: The unmodified dual-phase lamellar colonies of the eutectic high-entropy alloy, which typically exhibit high strength but limited tensile ductility due to microcrack initiation at sharp internal boundaries.
generation.boundary: The intervention is effective provided that the Nb addition remains within a narrow range (1–2 at.%) to avoid excess formation of brittle Nb-rich phases. The controlled slow cooling must be optimized to ensure coherent nanoprecipitate formation without coarsening or undesirable phase transformations. The hypothesis is expected to hold under typical room-temperature tensile conditions.
generation.uncertainty: While the hypothesized mechanism is supported by analogous behavior in microalloyed alloys, uncertainties remain regarding the precise kinetics of nanoprecipitate formation and their spatial distribution at the lamellar boundaries. There may also be sensitivities related to cooling rates and potential interactions with other alloying elements that require careful experimental verification.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the base eutectic AlCoCrFeNi alloy and one set microalloyed with 1–2 at.% Nb, both processed under identical controlled slow cooling conditions. Characterize the microstructure using high-resolution electron microscopy to verify the presence and distribution of Nb-rich nanoprecipitates at the lamellar boundaries. Perform room-temperature tensile tests on both sets to compare yield/ultimate tensile strength and ductility.
measurements: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) to confirm Nb segregation
Tensile testing to measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation to failure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Nb-microalloyed samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in both tensile strength and room-temperature ductility relative to the base alloy, or if the microstructural analysis fails to show the expected coherent nanoprecipitates at the lamellar boundaries, then the hypothesis is falsified.

proposals.intervention: Microalloying with trace Nb addition to promote interfacial nanoprecipitation
proposals.conditions: Melt the base alloy with 1–2 at.% Nb under vacuum induction melting followed by controlled slow cooling to allow Nb segregation and nanoprecipitate formation at the lamellar colony boundaries
proposals.structural_mediator: Formation of coherent Nb-rich nanoprecipitates at interphase boundaries
proposals.mechanism: Nb segregates to the internal boundaries, forming fine, coherent precipitates that strengthen the boundary regions by blocking crack initiation and impeding dislocation motion while simultaneously relieving local stress concentrations
proposals.predicted_outcome: Enhanced tensile strength through precipitation hardening combined with improved ductility owing to tougher, more ductile interfacial regions, relative to the baseline untreated lamellar structure
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This intervention directly targets the microcracking-prone dual-phase boundaries by reinforcing them, thus potentially overcoming the trade-off between strength and ductility found in conventional processing

proposals.intervention: Thermomechanical processing via cold rolling followed by short-time annealing
proposals.conditions: Apply ~50% cold rolling reduction at room temperature followed by an annealing treatment near the eutectic temperature (e.g., 800–850 °C for a short duration of 2–5 minutes) to refine the lamellar spacing
proposals.structural_mediator: Reduced lamellar colony spacing and enhanced interphase boundary adhesion
proposals.mechanism: Cold rolling initially introduces strain hardening and defects, and the subsequent short anneal leads to controlled recrystallization and boundary coarsening at a microscale level, reducing local stress concentrations while maintaining a refined dual-phase architecture
proposals.predicted_outcome: Both increased yield/ultimate tensile strength from strain hardening and improved ductility due to a more uniform and less brittle lamellar microstructure compared to the unmodified state
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By re-engineering the lamellar spacing and boundary condition, this single intervention mitigates the initiation of microcracks and distributes strain more evenly, addressing the brittleness issue without sacrificing strength

proposals.intervention: Gradient diffusion treatment to engineer graded interphase boundaries
proposals.conditions: Subject the cast alloy to a controlled heat treatment with a temperature gradient (e.g., 850–900 °C for several hours) enabling interdiffusion at the lamellar interfaces
proposals.structural_mediator: Gradually varying composition across the lamellar boundaries, resulting in smoother transition regions
proposals.mechanism: The controlled interdiffusion leads to graded interfacial zones that reduce abrupt composition or stiffness mismatches, thereby decreasing local stress concentrations and deferring crack nucleation and propagation
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved room-temperature tensile ductility by mitigating crack initiation and propagation while maintaining or even enhancing strength through a well-tailored interfacial structure, relative to the sharp, unmodified lamellar boundaries
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This strategy directly modifies the microstructural feature (interface abruptness) responsible for microcracking, thus offering a pathway to improve both strength and ductility in a single intervention

proposals.intervention: Rapid solidification processing to in situ generate a dispersion of coherent nanoprecipitates along lamellar interfaces
proposals.conditions: Employ melt spinning or high-pressure die casting to achieve cooling rates on the order of 10^5–10^6 K/s, ensuring a fine dispersion of nanoscale precipitates at the lamellar boundaries
proposals.structural_mediator: Uniform distribution of coherent nanoprecipitates at internal boundaries within the lamellar colonies
proposals.mechanism: The rapid cooling traps a high density of nanoprecipitates that simultaneously obstruct dislocation motion (increasing strength) and blunt crack tips at the boundaries (enhancing ductility), thereby minimizing microcrack formation
proposals.predicted_outcome: The alloy is expected to exhibit increased strength from precipitation strengthening coupled with improved tensile ductility due to enhanced interfacial toughness compared to conventionally processed lamellar colonies
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This single processing intervention leverages rapid solidification to tailor the microstructure at the critical boundaries, offering a simultaneous solution to both brittle failure and the conventional trade-off between strength and ductility

decision.rationale: Direction D (microalloying with trace Nb addition) directly targets the key microstructural weakness by promoting the formation of coherent Nb-rich nanoprecipitates at the critical internal boundaries in the eutectic high-entropy alloy. This intervention is attractive because it is a single, compositional modification that reinforces the interphase boundaries, thereby simultaneously improving strength (through precipitation hardening and dislocation impediment) and ductility (by reducing microcrack initiation). Compared to alternative approaches – which involve more complex processing steps (cold rolling with controlled annealing, gradient diffusion, or rapid solidification) – the Nb microalloying strategy offers a more straightforward path with a clear mechanism and favorable prior evidence in similar alloy systems.
